title: Hyperspectral Imaging for Noncontact Characterization of Organ Systems and Abdominal Diseases
summary: This study investigates a new imaging technique used during abdominal surgery. Using special light, the tissue is imaged without physical contact, revealing information that is not visible to the naked eye. In the future, these images will help doctors better distinguish between healthy and diseased tissue. In cancer surgeries or endometriosis procedures, this could help define resection margins more precisely and better preserve healthy tissue. The study itself poses no risk to patients, as it uses only harmless visible light.
conditions: Female patients who are candidates for laparoscopic and/or open gynecological surgery

interventions.name:
Female patients indicated for laparoscopic and/or open surgical procedures undergo intraoperative hyperspectral imaging using the TIVITA Mini System (KARL STORZ).
Procedure:
Contactless HSI imaging during the scheduled surgery (7.5 cm distance, ~7 seconds per measurement, wavelength range 500–1000

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Indications for laparoscopic and/or open surgery
- written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Anticipated noncompliance by the patient or the patient’s inability to understand the
nature and purpose of the clinical trial
- Lack of patient consent
- Existing pregnancy
